_comment: Synthetic fixtures. Deliberately not real memories: the eval is committed to a public repository, and real ones carry proprietary detail. Each scenario is a set of episodes as they would actually be recorded during work, plus the claim compaction produces from them. Keeping both lets retrieval over raw episodes be compared against retrieval over distilled claims on identical ground.

episodes.title: tests failed, 14 errors all connection refused
episodes.body: Checked the test database config, looked correct. Ports match.

episodes.title: reset the test database, still refused
episodes.body: Dropped and recreated. Same 14 failures. Not a data problem.

episodes.title: postgres container was not running
episodes.body: docker compose up fixed every failure immediately.

claim.title: Tests need `docker compose up` first
claim.body: Connection-refused failures in the test suite are almost always the missing postgres container rather than the test code or the database contents.

episodes.title: requests to /api/v2 are not authenticated
episodes.body: Handlers receive no user object. Works fine on v1.

episodes.title: v2 router registered before the auth middleware
episodes.body: Registration order in server.ts puts the router first, so middleware never runs for those paths.

episodes.title: moved middleware registration above the v2 router
episodes.body: Auth now applies. Added a test asserting 401 on an unauthenticated v2 call.

claim.title: Middleware must be registered before routers
claim.body: Anything registered after a router silently skips that middleware for its paths, so authentication is bypassed without any error. Register auth first in server.ts.

episodes.title: npm install fails with a lockfile mismatch
episodes.body: Peer dependency errors and an unresolvable tree.

episodes.title: npm ci also fails, lockfile is not npm's
episodes.body: There is a pnpm-lock.yaml in the root.

episodes.title: pnpm install works
episodes.body: Installs cleanly. The repo has always used pnpm.

claim.title: This repo uses pnpm, not npm
claim.body: `npm install` fails on a lockfile mismatch because the lockfile is pnpm-lock.yaml. Use `pnpm install`.

episodes.title: evaluated Prisma for the data layer
episodes.body: Good ergonomics, generated types are pleasant.

episodes.title: Prisma migrations do not fit our deploy
episodes.body: Shadow database is not available in the deploy environment and migrate deploy assumes it.

episodes.title: went with Kysely instead
episodes.body: Query builder only, migrations stay hand-written SQL under migrations/.

claim.title: We use Kysely, and rejected Prisma over migrations
claim.body: Prisma was rejected because its migration flow needs a shadow database that the deploy environment does not provide. Migrations are hand-written SQL under migrations/.

episodes.title: token expiry test fails only in CI
episodes.body: Passes locally every time. Fails maybe one run in three on CI.

episodes.title: CI machine clock is ahead of the token issuer
episodes.body: Skew of a few seconds is enough for the expiry assertion to flip.

episodes.title: froze the clock in test setup, green
episodes.body: Used fake timers in the setup file rather than widening the tolerance.

claim.title: Auth tests are clock-sensitive; freeze the clock in setup
claim.body: Intermittent CI failures in token tests are usually machine clock skew rather than logic. Freeze time in tests/setup.ts instead of loosening assertions.

episodes.title: stale prices shown after a catalogue update
episodes.body: Update lands in the database but the API keeps serving old values.

episodes.title: redis keys are never invalidated on write
episodes.body: Only a 15 minute TTL. Writers do not touch the cache at all.

episodes.title: added explicit invalidation in the writer
episodes.body: Delete the key in the same transaction as the write.

claim.title: Catalogue writes must invalidate the redis key
claim.body: The cache has only a TTL, so a write without explicit invalidation serves stale data for up to fifteen minutes. Delete the key in the same transaction as the write.
